rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī traces صال to following or rushing upon with force, citing the donkey driving its mate and a man or stallion attacking; related forms can mean mixing or gathering what was scattered.
rows.anchor: الذي يجيء عل إثر السابق , فإنه يواصله , وصلى الحمار أتنه : طردها وقحمها الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives union and joining as the semantic core of الوصلة, opposed to separation, and relates it to joints, joined things, relationships, and continuity.
rows.anchor: والوصلة - التي هي مدار المادة وكأنها الحقيقة التي تشعبت منها فروعها - هي الضم وهي التئام الشيء بالشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He extends connection and continuity through وصيلة: a ewe bearing a male then a female, linked garments, entangled yarn, broad land, and the final night connecting two months.
rows.anchor: والوصيلة : الشاة تلد ذكرا ثم تلد أنثى , فتصل الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Roasting is described as joining meat to fire; related forms mean casting into fire or heating a hand, while صليت فلانا means dealing with or deceiving him to secure his company.
rows.anchor: وصليت اللحم : شويته - لأنك وصلته بالنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms for putting something into fire, heating a hand, and enduring its heat derive from joining the object to fire.
rows.anchor: وأصليته النار : أدخلته إياها وأثويته فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الصلاية means the forehead because it repeatedly touches the ground in prayer, and also a perfume-pounder because it is repeatedly used for pounding.
rows.anchor: والصلاية - ويهمز : الجبهة , لكثرة مباشرتها الأرض في الصلاة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says Satan has snares and traps; Biqāʿī uses it to gloss مصالي as the plural of مصلاة, a snare, alongside فخ, a trap.
rows.anchor: ومنه الحديث ( إن للشيطان مصالي وفخوخا ) جمع مصلاة وفخ

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzāz describes al-ṣilyān as a plant with a large root, one of the best pastures, eaten by horses; Biqāʿī says it was named for camels’ frequent grazing on it.
rows.anchor: وقال القزاز : وهو شجر له جعثن ضخم , ربما جرد وسطه ونبت ما حوله

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: A reported gloss says لصيت الرجل means to accuse or reproach someone with sexual wrongdoing, while لصي إليه means to join him under suspicion.
rows.anchor: ولصيت الرجل كرميت ورضيت - إذا عبته وقذفته بالفجور , وقال القزاز : وقيل : هو أن يضيفه إلى ربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He records aṣla as a snake that attacks a person; the dictionaries differ on whether it is small or large, with the latter described as deadly by its breath.
rows.anchor: والأصلة - محركة : حية قصيرة تساورالإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several side forms express assault or motion: a camel may attack people, and a horse’s neigh is called صئيل because its notes continue in sequence.
rows.anchor: وصؤل البعير - ككرم صآلة : واثب الناس أو صار يقتل الناس ويعدو عليهم , وصئيل الفرس : صهيله - لمواصلة نغماته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣīl can denote someone of lineage, while aṣl is a foundation; the verb for becoming rooted also means becoming established or firm.
rows.anchor: والأصيل : من له أصل - ككرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-aṣī means evening, either as the link between day and night or as night itself; alternatively it signals day’s end, as if the day were uprooted from its source. The term also extends to death and destruction.
rows.anchor: والأصي : العشي - لأنه وصلة ما بين النهار والليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says his earlier discussion of the wording “your prayer commands you” in Hūd signals the same lexical point.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى عند قوله تعالى وفي سورة هود عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī reads the rain’s descent as an observable sign of God’s sovereignty: bringing water down at a chosen time and in great quantity makes the valleys flow.
rows.anchor: ولما كان حمل الماء في العلو لا يمكن إلا عن قهر , وإنزاله في وقت دون غيره كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wādī is a mountain slope facing another mountain or hill, where rain gathers and runs through the open space; the author links diya money to the great sum collected for homicide.
rows.anchor: والوادي : سفح الجبل العظيم الذي يقابله جبل أو تل فيجمع فيه المطر , فيجري في فضائه , ومنه أخذت الدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadr means proportioning one thing to another without excess or deficiency; the waters fill the valleys, showing God’s exclusive lordship and providing the parable’s first image.
rows.anchor: والقدر : اتزان الشيء بغيره من غير زيادة ولا نقصان , فالمعنى أن المياه ملأت الأودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zabad is foam that rises high because of its lightness; the same root covers sea and camel foam, fluffing cotton, and other forms of lightness, with speed sometimes following from it.
rows.anchor: أي عاليا بانتفاخه : والزبد : الرغوة التي تعلو الماء , ومدار المادة على الخفة , ويلزمها العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says foam is an apt likeness for the idols: it rises over water that gathers dirt, and also appears when pure solid metals are melted, yet it is transient in both cases.
rows.anchor: ولما الزبد أحسن مثل لمعبوداتهم , وكان لا يختص بالماء الذي هو مائع بطبعه بجمع الأوضار والأقذار

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān glosses jufāʾ as vanishing and disintegrating, with no benefit or permanence.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : أي مضمحلا متلاشيا لا منفعة فيه لا بقاء له

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī takes jufāʾ to mean dispersed, citing the wind cutting apart clouds as a usage of the related verb.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري : متفرقا , من جفأت الريح الغيم - إذا قطعته

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī explains jufāʾ as the staying of something in a place until it perishes.
rows.anchor: وقال الرماني : والجفاء : بنو مكان الشيء به حتى يهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Foam represents falsehood, doubts, suspicions, and the provocations of the obdurate: it may surge briefly as a test that distinguishes the steady from the shaken, then quickly vanishes.
rows.anchor: فهذا مثل الباطل من الشكوك والشبه وما أثاره أهل العناد , لا بقاء له وإن جال جولة

words: وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Useful water and metal represent truth: water sustains life, while metal supports livelihood and social dealings; the Qur’an gives life to hearts and preserves the religious law.
rows.anchor: فالماء والمعدن مثل القرآن لما فيه من حياة القلوب وبقاء الشرع كما أن الماء يحيى الأراضي الميتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Valleys and vessels represent hearts: each retains what it can according to its breadth or narrowness, purity, and strength of understanding.
rows.anchor: والأودية والأواني مثل القلوب يثبت منه فيها ما تحتمله على قدر سعة القلب وضيقه بحسب الطهارة وقوة الفاهمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second image is metal heated until it melts: people seek jewelry such as bracelets and rings, or useful goods such as coins, swords, and vessels, covering the categories of metalwork.
rows.anchor: تتحلون بها من الأساور والحلق ونحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The division between adornment and utility is comprehensive; it also conveys royal disdain for things people competitively prize, as kings display honor by treating them lightly.
rows.anchor: فهذا تقسيم حاصر لأنواع الفلز المنوه إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Foam clings to trees, valley sides, or a vessel’s rim and is removed, leaving the underlying substance pure, just as doubts and suspicions depart from truth.
rows.anchor: يكشط عن وجهه أو يعلق بأطراف الإناء فيذهب ويبقى ذلك الجوهر خالصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that God sets forth truth and falsehood by a parable of this kind; “striking” a parable is making it travel through lands for people to repeat and exemplify.
rows.anchor: وضرب المثل : تسييره في البلاد يتمثل به الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable’s clarity is so striking that the closing question is whether every matter can be made this clear; Biqāʿī answers that God makes parables clear even when their subjects are obscure.
rows.anchor: فيجعلها في غاية الوضوح وإن كانت في غاية الغموض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across its ordered forms and roots, j-f-ʾ turns on casting or throwing away: foam is cast out, scum wiped off a pot or valley, a person thrown down, and plants uprooted.
rows.anchor: ومادة ( جفا ) - واوية ويائية مهموزة وغير مهموزة بكل ترتيب , وهي جفأ جأف فجأ , جفي جيف فيج , جفو جوف فوج , فجو وجف - تدور على الطرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root family also yields j-afāʾ as a vacated or empty ship, and forms for abandonment, separation from one’s place, heaviness, and coarse, non-adhering character.
rows.anchor: جفا الشيء يجفو - إذا لم يلزم مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jawf denotes a hollow that can receive and hold what is cast into it: a hollow in the land or body, the middle of night, and a spacious container; related forms include a cavity-reaching wound.
rows.anchor: ومن واوية : الجوف : المطمئن من الأرض , لأنه يسع ما يطرح فيه ويمسكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The f-j-ʾ family suggests something suddenly thrown upon a person; its related فجوة is open ground or a gap prepared to receive what is cast into it.
rows.anchor: فجئه الأمر - كسمعه ومنعه : هجم عليه من غير أن يشعر , كأنه قذف به إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other inverted forms cover a messenger who moves swiftly, a group cut off from a larger crowd, scent spreading, and the restless motion of camels or horses; Biqāʿī relates them to throwing or movement.
rows.anchor: ومنه الفيج - لرسول السلطان على رجليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human creation is an especially strong proof of divine oneness and deliberate action: the human is the noblest body in the lower world and cannot be nobler than its Lord.
rows.anchor: أي هذا النوع الذي خلقه أدل ما يكون على الوحدانية والفعل بالاختيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans surpass other animals through the noble powers of outward and inward senses, appetite and anger, and speech, which grasps universals and works with analogical reasoning.
rows.anchor: الحواس الظاهرة والباطنة , والشهوة والغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam was created from unqualified water, whereas his descendants were created from specific, ejaculated fluid.
rows.anchor: أي آدم عليه السلام من مطلق الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human made from humble water becomes eloquent and skilled in disputation, displaying speech and understanding despite having had no sensation or voluntary movement before.
rows.anchor: خصيم } أي منطيق عارف بالمجادلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transformation from inert fluid to an articulate disputant proves the creator’s complete power and choice; the one who originated humanity can also restore it.
rows.anchor: أفلا يقدر الذي ابتدأ ذلك على إعادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock are the eight pairs: sheep, goats, camels, and cattle; although larger and stronger than humans, they do not speak or explain themselves.
rows.anchor: أي الأزواج الثمانية : الضأن والمعز والإبل والبقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gifts are ordered from clothing that wards off cold, to their wider benefits including milk, then to food; warmth comes first because clothing is usually the first benefit people encounter.
rows.anchor: ولما كان أول ما يمكن أن يلقى الإنسان عادة من نعمها اللباس , بدأ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting “from them” first stresses that food from other sources scarcely counts beside food from livestock.
rows.anchor: وقدم الظرف دلالة على أن الأكل من غيرها بالنسبة إلى الأكل منها مما لا يعتد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After practical benefits, livestock’s beauty is presented as an additional, culminating benefit especially enjoyed by people.
rows.anchor: ثم تلاه بالتجمل لأنه النهاية لكونه للرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return from pasture is mentioned before the morning departure because it is more impressive and joyful than setting out.
rows.anchor: ولما كان القدوم أجل نعمة وأبهج من النزوج , قدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At evening return, full udders, tall humps, the movement of animals and herders, milking, and answering bleats and bellows make a striking spectacle and comfort for their owners.
rows.anchor: من الحلب والتردد لأجله وتجاوب الثغاء والرغاء

words: وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنَا فِى كُلِّ أُمَّةٍۢ رَّسُولًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the preceding plural “messengers” implies distribution among communities, this verse makes that distribution explicit, answers the expected question, rebuts objections to sending messengers, consoles the Prophet, and urges reflection.
rows.anchor: ولما كان جمع الرسل مفهما لتوزيعهم على الأمم , كان موضع توقع التصريح بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent a messenger to every earlier nation; Biqāʿī states that no one on earth was left unreached by the call.
rows.anchor: من الأمم الذين قبلكم { رسولا } فما بقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not say that the messenger was “from among them,” since messengers could address people outside their own community: Lot and Shuʿayb among the people of al-Aykah, and Solomon among those beyond Israel.
rows.anchor: ولأجل أن الرسل قد تكون من غير المرسل إليهم كلوط وشعيب عليهما السلام في أصحاب الأيكة وسليمان عليه السلام في غير بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers went to their peoples proclaiming worship of God alone and strenuous avoidance of false gods, as commanded by God’s messenger.
rows.anchor: أي الملك الأعلى وحده { واجتنبوا } أي بكل جهدكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nations divided: God guided some to truth, who saw it and obeyed the callers and thereby merited Paradise; others had error fixed upon them and incurred punishment.
rows.anchor: فكان من غير شك بعضهم مرض لله وبعضهم مغضب له , فإنه لا يكون حكم المتنافيين واحدا أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī distinguishes divine command, which may not be fulfilled, from divine will, which necessarily occurs; the misguided reject the command but act within what God wills.
rows.anchor: فإن الأمر قد لا يكون ما تعلق به , والإرادة لا بد أن يكون ما تعلقت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If everything willed by God were morally right, both groups would be right and neither could be punished; instead, the disobedient were punished and the obedient saved in every nation, as the messengers said.
rows.anchor: فلو كان كل ما شاءه حقا كان الفريقان محقين فلم يعذب أحدهما , لكنه لم يكن الأمر كذلك , بل عذب العاصي ونجى الطائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast establishes the truthfulness of the messengers and the falsehood of their opponents; those who disobeyed had no remaining excuse to defend themselves.
rows.anchor: فدل ذلك قطعا على صدق الرسل وكذب مخالفيهم , فالآية من الاحتباك
